hero.subText: Type-First Build Compilation with Runtime Orchestration
hero.description: Pristine TypeScript types compiled into live runtime blueprints. Zero schema duplication, zero bundle inflation.

blockOne.description: Xalor is a build-time TypeScript engine that transforms native types into a live runtime system for validation, generation, and transformation — without duplicating schemas or shipping heavy validation libraries.

blockTwo.description: Unlike **Zod** or **Yup** which require writing heavy runtime schemas, or macro generators like **Typia** which clutter your git history with generated files, Xalor uses a silent background compiler watcher to turn pristine TypeScript interfaces into optimized runtime maps.
list: _The Result_ Use them natively at runtime.

one.description: Handle external API inputs cleanly with flexible runtime safety boundaries.

two.description: Generate type-safe mocks, staging state objects, or default templates out of thin air.

three.description: Manipulate object shapes inline at runtime using type properties as commands.

four.description: Eliminate the manual schema-updating workflow forever. When you modify your interface, your runtime behavior changes natively on the very next compilation step.

installation.description: Set up the core package using your preferred node dependency tool chain.

list: Eliminates the _Dual-Source Tax_- Write your data definitions precisely once. Stop maintaining matching type interfaces and validation schemas concurrently.
Massive Client Bundle Reduction- Moves data model parsing completely to the build stage. Production apps inherit tiny metadata maps rather than thousands of lines of heavy validation parsing logic.
GPS Telemetry Traceability- When an object fails matching rules, Xalor flags the exact file path and line location of the target TypeScript source code instead of throwing unhelpful generic errors.

header.description: A high-performance type engine that reads your native TypeScript definitions to handle automatic, ultra-fast data validation at runtime—with zero code bloat, zero duplicate schemas, and zero background resource waste.

singleSourceOfTruth.description: Every other validation framework forces you into a _double-maintenance tax_ You have to manually write a custom runtime validation schema language blocks (like a Zod schema) and then write a mirrored TypeScript interface right next to it just to get autocompletion.
singleSourceOfTruth.subDescription: Xalor treats your standard, everyday TypeScript types as the absolute, **single source of truth**. You write a standard type, pass it to Xalor's proxy handle, and the engine takes over. If you modify or delete a type property, your workspace data layers adapt instantly with **hard-zero duplication overhead**.

codeBlock.note: By evaluating the native TypeScript _Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)_ directly in memory, Xalor allows your actual development types to serve as your operational enforcement gates. There are no secondary validation libraries to import into your source files, no runtime parsing definitions to synchronize, and zero opportunities for **manual drift** between your compile-time contracts and runtime validation bounds.

phantomBuild.description: Legacy validation frameworks ruin client performance by shipping thousands of lines of heavy, nested JavaScript schema definitions directly to the browser. As your application models scale from **10 to 500**, your production bundles bloat with un-tree-shakable validation logic that crushes your _Google Lighthouse scores_.
phantomBuild.subDescription: Xalor solves this using a _Hybrid Architecture Split_: a background watcher extracts and hashes your TypeScript AST into an isolated server-side **CAS map**, completely erasing the type telemetry to guarantee **absolute zero bundle inflation**.

codeBlock.note: Look closely at the `amount` rows inside **both** `sh_16c0mbs` and `sh_1nculbp`. Instead of copy-pasting duplicate structural logic across thousands of endpoints, the engine maps both parent configurations directly to a single shared layout vault token (`sh_1cr65y8`). Your project pays the memory assignment tax exactly once.

compilerAudit.description: Traditional frameworks leave you blind to your application's actual data footprint, allowing dead type schemas and silent contract drift to pile up. Xalor exposes this layer completely via a native background toolchain watcher—protecting your machine from local process collisions while delivering bare-metal terminal diagnostics.
compilerAudit.subDescription: While the _Ghost Emitter_ dynamically streams updated tracking keys directly into your IDE autocomplete maps behind the scenes using **Atomic Shield OS rename protections**, running `npx xalor audit` forces complete architectural visibility. This profiler outputs a real-time ledger tracking structural compaction data, **metadata evaporation deltas**, and exact call-site orphan locations.

image.note: High-fidelity rendering of the Xalor Operational Profiler Report. The dark-mode graphical card maps out real-time compiler telemetry: storage compaction ratios, lifecycle metadata evaporation metrics demonstrating 56.9% fat stripped away from production distribution files, and a clean API contract drift ledger state.

codeBlock.note: Xalor handles workspace scaling challenges behind the scenes. While traditional compiler plugins constantly crash local language servers by rewriting messy, bloated physical code structures into your working project folders, Xalor locks down your caching files with isolated atomic OS rename updates. It pipes autocomplete metadata straight into ambient memory modules, keeping your source repository pristine and your local save cycles completely collision-free.

typeGraphTelemetry.description: Validation is just a beneficial side-effect. By extracting deep, structural compile-time metadata, Xalor answers the ultimate question: 'What else can you do with types?' It unlocks an entire ecosystem of **live code tracking**, automated mock simulations, and real-time visual infrastructure analytics.
typeGraphTelemetry.subDescription: While our local orchestration web console is finalizing, running `npx xalor studio` forces your background toolchain to map out your entire structural schema network. The background compiler serializes your internal contract dependencies into an isomorphic graph matrix—ready to pipe directly into live **3D relationship lineages** or instant mock data factories.

codeBlock.note:
Because Xalor has already extracted and compiled your complete codebase type topology into content-addressed primitive objects, your types unlock an extensible infrastructure layer. Pass your reference keys natively into our 6 core runtime strategy vectors:

• _xalor.parse_: Executes high-velocity structural verification returning typed data.
• _xalor.guard_: Functions as a bare-metal assertive inline type gate passing unknown objects safely.
• _xalor.match_: Evaluates polymorphic payload webhooks directly into strongly-typed closure handlers.
• _xalor.default_: Instantly hydrates local unit test suites using clean, zero-config factory data records.
• _xalor.merge_: Combines separate, pre-compiled AST structural blueprints together on the fly in memory.
• _xalor.clone_: Performs deep memory object duplication while fully preserving internal structural type identity.

empiricalBenchmarks.description: We don't ask you to take our word for it. When evaluated down to **execution velocity** and **bundle impact**, Xalor strips away the performance penalties of traditional validation libraries to deliver true **bare-metal efficiency**.
empiricalBenchmarks.subDescription: By executing type unrolling entirely at _compilation phase_ rather than evaluating properties dynamically at runtime, data processing checks bypass overhead completely. Contrast your project specs directly against industry baselines across bundle sizes and validation speeds to see the architectural **performance deltas** live.

registerType.description: Registration can happen in one of two ways. Either through a simple type declaration and injection or through simply passing the data object you'd like to register as a type.
registerType.subDescription: Whether using explicit generic bindings or inline object inferences, Xalor’s compile-time scanner intercepts the target structural graph and provisions a unique Content-Addressable Storage (CAS) pointer hash inside your shadow type registry. This completely separates developer-facing type telemetry from the production-ready application distribution assets.

validateWithParse.header: Validate Your Data, Not Like Everyone Else
validateWithParse.description: Traditional packages execute heavy, recursive graph traversals over human-maintained validation sheets at runtime. Xalor bypasses runtime graph generation entirely by utilizing the pre-compiled build blueprints. Unknown payloads pass through a strict, linear properties assessment using lightning-fast property matches and direct pointer evaluation.
validateWithParse.subDescription: When an incoming payload violates a structural layout boundary, the parsing phase aborts instantly without allocating unnecessary error objects in RAM. The execution flow automatically routes the validation exception directly into the Auditor Telemetry Pipeline, identifying the exact line file origin of the target TypeScript contract.

exploreOtherApis.description: Validation is merely the entry gate. Leverage the unified type-graph infrastructure to trigger automated client SDK generation, orchestrate instant zero-maintenance test seed factories, or spin up live schema drift monitors using the local developer dashboard framework.
exploreOtherApis.subDescription: Xalor breaks away from the industry-wide misconception that types are disposable, build-only artifacts or simple guardrails for validation rules. We treat your TypeScript architecture as a rich, multi-dimensional source of system intelligence. By saving and content-addressing the deep Abstract Syntax Tree relationships, a single source type model shifts from a static text file into a dynamic runtime primitive capable of generating self-healing infrastructure, deterministic simulation pools, and automated client layers.

contentList.description: Generates a stateless **type predicate closure** for sub-microsecond payload narrowing at runtime boundaries.

contentList.name: parse
contentList.description: Synchronously evaluates incoming shapes against blueprints, throwing **traceable GPS diagnostics** on failure.

contentList.name: default
contentList.description: Manufactures **safe fallback structures** pre-hydrated with system primitives to prevent undefined crashes.

contentList.name: clone
contentList.description: Performs a **deep, circular-safe copy** while physically scrubbing away keys missing from blueprints.

contentList.name: merge
contentList.description: Fuses schemas symmetrically; matching primitives overwrite, nested objects fuse, and arrays combine item-by-item.

contentList.name: drift
contentList.description: Audits live system payloads to identify and log **structural schema mutations** against baselines.

contentList.name: composite
contentList.description: Combines multiple **independent registry contracts** into a unified validation execution graph.

contentList.name: cast
contentList.description: Forces loose external payload structures into compliance by safely mapping mismatched **primitive variants**.

contentList.description: Computes a flat **structural delta matrix** contrasting property discrepancies across two active shapes.
